The wrong pair is (4) Karl Marx - 'Discourse on the Method'.

'Discourse on the Method' was written by René Descartes. It is the book in which he gave his rules of research, including the rule that one should never accept anything for true till all grounds of doubt are excluded. The book written by Karl Marx is 'Das Kapital', a treatise which is the most referred book all over the world.

The other three pairs are correct. Hegel's well known book is 'Reason in History'; a collection of Leopold von Ranké's articles is published as 'The Theory and Practice of History'; and the Greek historian Herodotus used the term 'History' first for his book entitled 'The Histories'.

Dialectics is a method of analysis which is based on opposites, given by Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel. According to Hegel, the meaning of any event is grasped in terms of two direct opposites, such as True-False or Good-Bad, and the human mind cannot understand the true nature of an event without understanding these opposites. In this method a theory is proposed at the beginning, which is called 'Thesis'. Then another theory, contrary to the thesis, is proposed, which is called 'Antithesis'. After a thorough logical discussion of both, a new thesis is proposed which includes the gist of both the thesis and the antithesis, and this process of arriving at the new thesis is called 'Synthesis'.

The 'Annales School' is a new school of historiography that arose in France at the onset of the twentieth century. It was started by French historians. The Annales School gave a new direction to history writing. Because of it, it was recognised that history is not only about political events, kings, great leaders and accordingly politics, diplomacy and wars, but also about the climate, local people, agriculture, trade, technology, means of communication, social divisions and their collective psychology in the historical times. In this way the school widened the subject matter of history to cover all aspects of the life of ordinary people.

This happened because of feminist historiography, which means the restructuring of history from the perspective of women. Feminist historiography emphasised not only the inclusion of women in history, but also the rethinking of the male dominated perspective of history. Once history was looked at from the point of view of women, the ordinary details of women's lives became worth studying. Therefore historical research was driven to focus in depth on various aspects of women's life, such as their employment, their role in trade unions, the institutions working for their cause and their family life. In the historical writings after 1990 women were portrayed as an independent social class.

Michel Foucault argued in his book 'Archaeology of Knowledge' that the prevailing practice of arranging historical events in a chronological order is not right. He drew attention to the fact that archaeology does not strive to reach the ultimate historical truth, but attempts to explain the various transitions in the past. Foucault felt that explaining the transitions in history is more important than arranging events in order or searching for one final truth. Because his own method worked in this same way, he called it 'the archaeology of knowledge'.

In the latter half of the nineteenth century a new school of thought arose keeping in view the new thesis formulated by Karl Marx (1818-1883). According to Karl Marx, history was not about abstract ideas; it was about living people. He held that human relationships are shaped by the fundamental needs of people, and by the ownership as well as the nature of the prevalent means of production used to meet those needs. The accessibility of these means of production to the different strata of society may not be equal. This inequality causes a division of the society into classes, and that division leads to class struggle. The class that owns the means of production economically exploits the rest of the classes. Therefore, according to Marx, human history is the history of class struggle. 'Das Kapital', a treatise written by him, is the most referred book all over the world.

The four main characteristics of modern historiography are:

(1) Its method is based on scientific principles. It begins with the formation of relevant questions.

(2) These questions are anthropocentric. It means that these questions are about the deeds of the members of ancient human societies of a particular period. History does not suggest any interrelation between the Divine and human deeds.

(3) The answers to these questions are supported by reliable evidence.

(4) History presents a graph of mankind's journey with the help of past human deeds.

It is said that modern historiography with these characteristics has its roots in the ancient Greek historical writings.

Feminist historiography means the restructuring of history from the perspective of women. The writings of Simone de Beauvoir helped in establishing the fundamentals of feminism. She was French. Feminist historiography emphasised not only the inclusion of women in history, but also the rethinking of the male dominated perspective of history. It drove historical research to focus in depth on various aspects of women's life, such as their employment, their role in trade unions, the institutions working for their cause and their family life. In the historical writings after 1990 women were portrayed as an independent social class.

Leopold von Ranké (1795-1886) was of Berlin University, and the historiography of the nineteenth century was greatly influenced by his thoughts. He spoke about the critical method of historical research. He put emphasis on the utmost importance of the information gathered through original documents. He also stated that all types of documents associated with a historical event need to be examined with the greatest care. He believed that with this method it was possible to reach the historical truth. He criticised the imaginative narration of history. A collection of his articles is published in two books, entitled 'The Theory and Practice of History' and 'The Secret of World History'.
